incidents.victim: Telecom carriers and subscribers (Taiwan primarily, 6 countries)
incidents.vector: The newly identified group "SilentAir" hacks telco infrastructure and plants backdoors that run malicious SS7 and Diameter signaling-protocol commands to track subscriber locations and intercept calls and SMS traffic.
incidents.impact: Active since early 2025 across telcos in six countries, the group has mostly targeted Taiwanese carriers and subscribers, with rare targeting of VIPs such as political figures and government officials.

incidents.victim: Managed service providers and customers (~50 organizations, 288+ endpoints)
incidents.vector: An intruder abused a third-party ConnectWise ScreenConnect extension called RMM+, which in two versions defaulted to accepting a blank access key, to push commands that silently installed rogue ScreenConnect clients and a toolkit dubbed SCKit onto managed endpoints.
incidents.impact: At least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations were compromised within 90 minutes; SCKit established persistence and included a component designed to target connecting technicians' workstations, prompting ConnectWise to disable the extension across roughly 400 partner environments.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency/Web3 individuals and open-source software maintainers
incidents.vector: North Korean hackers (publicly known as Sapphire Sleet, BlueNoroff and APT38) lure targets into video calls, play prerecorded or deepfake footage of trusted contacts to build confidence, then trick the victim into installing malware via a fake "technical fix."
incidents.impact: The scheme, dubbed FaceStealer, has stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months and increasingly targets open-source maintainers to enable software supply-chain attacks; the FBI seized cloud infrastructure containing over 900 victim webcam recordings used to impersonate victims.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached ActiveCloud's systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure in a ransomware attack.
incidents.impact: Corporate websites, email and virtual servers used by businesses across Belarus were disrupted for days; the attack follows similar recent incidents at Russian hosting providers ESTT (ransomware) and Beget (destructive data-wiping), though no link between the three has been confirmed.

incidents.vector: Not yet disclosed; Polish officials say evidence points to involvement by foreign adversaries.
incidents.impact: Poland temporarily suspended the ePUAP e-government portal, used for public administrative services nationwide, while IT teams investigate and restore it.

incidents.vector: Not yet disclosed; hackers breached a website FSEC uses for financial institutions to submit security assessments.
incidents.impact: Personal data was stolen from South Korea's financial security agency, which confirmed the breach in a public statement.

incidents.victim: Supermarkets, medical facilities and US military commissaries (France, Belgium, Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Estonia, US)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-exposed refrigeration control panels, using weak or default credentials to remotely set units to defrost mode and push temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F).
incidents.impact: Hundreds of supermarkets across France and 10+ other European countries had to discard spoiled food, some units caught fire, and a French national blood service's fridges were also targeted (no blood spoilage reported); French authorities formally attributed the October French wave to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, though other waves carry only low-confidence or alternate (Russia-linked hacktivist) attribution.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed internet-exposed equipment at the port, triggering a power outage that expanded into a broader compromise of the IT network.
incidents.impact: The port has operated on manual procedures for five days; some systems, including internet and telephone connectivity, have since been restored. The same port authority was separately targeted by the n0n data-extortion group in October after refusing a $26 million ransom demand.
More than 72,000 passport scans were stolen from Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka and ~400 Arara/TKC customers (incl. Sega)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Arara's email distribution service, used by TKC Corporation to operate administrative platforms for Japanese municipalities and other customers, then used the access to send mass phishing emails impersonating financial institutions.
incidents.impact: More than 77 million email addresses were exposed across nearly 400 Arara customers; Osaka City alone confirmed over 1 million residents' email addresses were leaked, part of a broader surge of attacks prompting Japan's government to announce $62 million in emergency cybersecurity funding.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Binance developer systems via a trojanized Homebrew download and a fake job-interview "coding assignment," then used stolen signing privileges to install a malicious Ethereum smart-account (EIP-7702) authorization that let them sweep wallet funds.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was transferred out of at least 11 Binance wallets, the largest crypto theft in history; the FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, and U.S. authorities have frozen over $2.7 billion and obtained court authorization to seize more than $1.2 billion of the stolen funds.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers with internet-facing management interfaces
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access on exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Roughly 0.02% of Palo Alto Networks' global install base — those with internet-facing management interfaces — were affected; the vendor contacted each impacted customer individually, while an estimated 1.9 million internet-facing PHP services worldwide remain on vulnerable versions.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense and semiconductor/telecom organizations (200+ organizations, 14 countries)
incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor used the open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX to run parallel, automated attacks against web applications, cloud services, VPNs and mail infrastructure at machine speed.
incidents.impact: Over an 11-day span the actor targeted more than 200 organizations across 14 countries, with confirmed post-exploitation access at nine, including two foreign ministries in Latin America and a Middle Eastern interior ministry.

incidents.vector: After compromising ConnectWise application credentials, the actor used the ARTEX AI framework to automate password-spraying sign-in attempts against downstream customer tenants.
incidents.impact: More than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants were targeted with accelerated sign-in attacks, with follow-on activity involving Microsoft Graph abuse, application credential theft and privilege changes.

incidents.victim: VPN appliance owners (SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet) in US & Europe
incidents.vector: The group known as TAG-218 compromised internet-facing VPN appliances — including via a Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) — then pivoted to the VMware ESXi hypervisor layer using a new post-exploitation framework called GhostFrame to harvest credentials and deploy ransomware.
incidents.impact: At least four victimized organizations were subsequently listed on the Settra ransomware leak site; GhostFrame gives operators centralized control over multiple hosted virtual machines from a single compromised ESXi host.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor, defense and civil-society organizations (19 organizations)
incidents.vector: Chinese-speaking attackers paired the open-source AI penetration-testing framework Cairn with Chinese models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek to autonomously plan and execute 25 intrusion operations against a given target and goal.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained unauthorized access or exfiltrated data from 10 of 19 targeted organizations, including over a million exposed records at a teachers' union, modification of a live industry standards-ballot document, and creation of persistent admin accounts at a semiconductor company.
